title: How close relationships keep us healthy and happy, with Richard Slatcher, PhD

sentences.en: Ask most people about the things that are important to them, about what really matters in their life and what makes them happy, and you'll hear a common refrain,
sentences.zh: 问问大多数人什么对他们来说很重要，什么才是生活中真正重要的，什么能让他们感到幸福，你会听到一个共同的答案：

sentences.en: my spouse or partner, my children, my family, my closest friends.
sentences.zh: 我的配偶或伴侣、我的孩子、我的家人、我最亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: Close relationships are essential to our happiness and well-being, and decades of research have shown that they're also important predictors of physical health.
sentences.zh: 亲密关系对我们的幸福和健康至关重要，几十年的研究表明，它们也是身体健康的重要预测指标。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: What kind of support do we receive from our partners and other close relationships, and why does that support matter so much?
sentences.zh: 我们从伴侣和其他亲密关系中得到了什么样的支持？为什么这种支持如此重要？

sentences.en: What are the biological mechanisms that tie together social relationships and health?
sentences.zh: 将社会关系与健康联系在一起的生物学机制是什么？

sentences.en: What are the ingredients of a good and supportive relationship, and how do we develop these deep ties to each other?
sentences.zh: 一段良好且相互支持的关系包含哪些要素？我们如何建立这些深厚的情感纽带？

sentences.en: Also, how has the COVID-19 pandemic affected our close relationships?
sentences.zh: 此外，新冠疫情对我们的亲密关系产生了怎样的影响？

sentences.en: Are people coming out of the past year and a half feeling a stronger connection to their loved ones, or have those ties frayed?
sentences.zh: 人们在过去一年半之后，是感觉与亲人的联系更紧密了，还是这些纽带已经变得脆弱？

sentences.en: And what, if any, lasting effects might we see?
sentences.zh: 如果有什么持久的影响，我们可能会看到什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Richard Slatcher, a professor of psychology and head of the Close Relationships Laboratory at the University of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是理查德·斯莱彻博士，他是佐治亚大学心理学教授，也是亲密关系实验室的负责人。

sentences.en: He studies how our intimate relationships get under our skin to affect our health and well-being, how people come to feel close to each other, and how technology,
sentences.zh: 他研究我们的亲密关系如何深入我们的内心从而影响我们的健康和幸福，人们如何变得亲密，以及科技，

sentences.en: like smartphones and social media, may be affecting our closest relationships.
sentences.zh: 比如智能手机和社交媒体，可能如何影响我们最亲密的关系。

sentences.en: For the past year, he's also been running a study called Love in the Time of COVID that's looked at how people's relationships have been faring through the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，他一直在进行一项名为“新冠时期的爱”的研究，观察人们的关系在疫情期间是如何发展的。

sentences.en: We'll try to discuss all of that today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天将尝试讨论所有这些话题。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Slatcher.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，斯莱彻博士。

sentences.en: It's great to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，金。

sentences.en: It might seem kind of obvious that good relationships make us happier, but as I just mentioned a few moments ago,
sentences.zh: 良好的关系让我们更幸福，这似乎显而易见，但正如我刚才提到的，

sentences.en: there are many years of research now suggesting that they make us healthier, too.
sentences.zh: 现在有许多年的研究表明，它们也能让我们更健康。

sentences.en: So let's start with a broad question.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从一个宏观的问题开始。

sentences.en: How and why are relationships important to our health and well-being?
sentences.zh: 关系如何以及为何对我们的健康和幸福如此重要？

sentences.en: What's the scientific evidence?
sentences.zh: 有什么科学证据吗？

sentences.en: I guess let's start with the well-being question.
sentences.zh: 我想我们先从幸福感的问题开始吧。

sentences.en: When you opened this segment, it reminded me of one of my intellectual heroes who passed away this year, Ed Diener, at the University of Illinois,
sentences.zh: 当你开启这个话题时，让我想起了我的一位智识导师，他今年去世了，他是伊利诺伊大学的埃德·迪纳，

sentences.en: who was really the father of happiness research.
sentences.zh: 他确实是幸福研究之父。

sentences.en: And it was his research that really pointed us to how important social relationships are for our well-being.
sentences.zh: 正是他的研究真正向我们指出了社会关系对我们的幸福有多么重要。

sentences.en: And he showed that all of the people who indicate on a 1 to 10 scale that they're at the most happy 10,
sentences.zh: 他表明，所有在1到10分的量表上表示自己最幸福（即10分）的人，

sentences.en: all of them to a person indicate having a close friend in their lives.
sentences.zh: 无一例外地表示他们的生活中有一个亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: And it's research that like that that's really kept me going because time and time again, we see how important our relationships are for how happy we are.
sentences.zh: 正是这样的研究一直支撑着我，因为我们一次又一次地看到，人际关系对我们的幸福感有多么重要。

sentences.en: And increasingly, we're finding out for how healthy we are, too.
sentences.zh: 而且我们越来越发现，它对我们的健康也同样重要。

sentences.en: I once gave a talk about five years or so in an interdisciplinary conference, a small meeting, and the person before me was an exercise physiologiSt.
sentences.zh: 大约五年前，我在一次跨学科会议上做过演讲，那是一个小型会议，在我之前发言的是一位运动生理学家。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of their talk, they said, I challenge anyone to argue with me about the importance of physical activity.
sentences.zh: 在演讲开始时，他说：“我挑战任何人来反驳我关于体育锻炼重要性的观点。”

sentences.en: You can't overstate the importance of physical activity.
sentences.zh: 体育锻炼的重要性怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: And I came up and I talked next and I said, I don't mean to try to top you,
sentences.zh: 接下来轮到我发言，我说：“我并不是想盖过你的风头，

sentences.en: but and then I showed her a graph of basically all of the different things that are associated with longevity, including not smoking, including physical activity,
sentences.zh: 但是……”然后我向她展示了一张图表，基本上涵盖了所有与长寿相关的因素，包括不吸烟、体育锻炼、

sentences.en: including not being fairly low weight and things like that.
sentences.zh: 包括体重不至于过低等等。

sentences.en: And right at the top was our social relationships.
sentences.zh: 而排在最顶端的正是我们的社会关系。

sentences.en: And it's it's a pretty robust finding that people who are more socially connected live longer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常稳健的发现，即社会联系更紧密的人寿命更长。

sentences.en: And there are all kinds of fascinating studies.
sentences.zh: 而且有各种各样的迷人研究。

sentences.en: There's a great study that you might have heard of called the nuns study, where they studied these nuns over several decades.
sentences.zh: 有一个很棒的研究，你可能听说过，叫“修女研究”，他们研究了这些修女几十年。

sentences.en: And nuns are a great group to study because they all live in the same environment, physical environment.
sentences.zh: 修女是一个很好的研究群体，因为她们都生活在相同的物理环境中。

sentences.en: So you're controlling for a lot of extraneous factors.
sentences.zh: 所以你控制了许多无关因素。

sentences.en: And by a mile, the nuns who had the closest relationships live the longer longest and the nuns who are the happiest live the longeSt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，关系最亲密的修女寿命最长，最幸福的修女也活得最久。

sentences.en: And we've seen this in the Harvard men's study, you know, that that's been going on for close to 100 years now.
sentences.zh: 我们在哈佛大学的男性研究中也看到了这一点，你知道，这项研究已经进行了近100年了。

sentences.en: And so it's really these kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，确实是这些，你知道，

sentences.en: the early work in this area that to me was so compelling that that got me to shift from just studying the basics of what makes relationships tick and what makes relationships succeed and fail to really how they're they they they are tied to why we are happy and healthy.
sentences.zh: 这一领域早期的工作对我来说非常有说服力，这促使我从仅仅研究关系运作的基本原理、关系成功与失败的原因，转向研究它们如何与我们为何幸福健康紧密相连。

sentences.en: Much of your research has focused specifically on marriages and other long-term intimate relationships.
sentences.zh: 你的大部分研究都专门针对婚姻和其他长期亲密关系。

sentences.en: Are these benefits true for other close relationships, too?
sentences.zh: 这些益处也适用于其他亲密关系吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you just talked about nuns, so they must be right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才谈到了修女，所以她们一定是正确的。

sentences.en: I mean, because nuns aren't married, they're married to Jesus, they're married to God.
sentences.zh: 因为修女没有结婚，她们嫁给了耶稣，嫁给了上帝。

sentences.en: But what about other close friendships and family relationships?
sentences.zh: 但是其他的亲密友谊和家庭关系呢？

sentences.en: Are the benefits that people derive equivalent to the benefits that they might get from a long-term intimate partner?
sentences.zh: 人们从中获得的益处是否等同于他们从长期亲密伴侣那里获得的益处？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, when I think about the size of the effects that we see for intimate relationships, and we did what's called a meta-analysis or an analysis of many papers,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我想到我们在亲密关系中看到的效应大小时，我们做了一个所谓的“荟萃分析”，即对许多论文进行了分析，

sentences.en: all the papers that have been done at the time, this is about five years ago, on the links between marital satisfaction and longevity.
sentences.zh: 当时所有的相关论文，大约是五年前，关于婚姻满意度与长寿之间的联系。

sentences.en: And when you look at other studies that have looked at just social connectedness in terms of how integrated you are with your social network,
sentences.zh: 当你观察其他研究时，那些仅仅从你与社交网络的整合程度来看社会联系的研究，

sentences.en: the social network findings are actually bigger.
sentences.zh: 社交网络的发现实际上更大。

sentences.en: So, although your marriage, if you are married, really impacts your physical health, those other close relationships that we have are enormously important, too.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然你的婚姻（如果你已婚的话）确实会影响你的身体健康，但我们拥有的其他亲密关系也极其重要。

sentences.en: And I say close relationships because those are the ones that we've studied, like marriage, friendships to a lesser extent, parent-child relationships to a greater extent.
sentences.zh: 我之所以说“亲密关系”，是因为这些是我们研究过的，比如婚姻，友谊（程度稍轻），亲子关系（程度更深）。

sentences.en: Not really one of the things I've become interested in actually during the pandemic is the importance of non-close relationships.
sentences.zh: 其实，我在疫情期间开始感兴趣的一件事是“非亲密关系”的重要性。

sentences.en: You know, that's something that we've, a lot of us have loSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是我们很多人都失去的东西。

sentences.en: But yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，绝对重要。

sentences.en: Friendships, for example, just matter so much.
sentences.zh: 例如，友谊就非常重要。

sentences.en: Ed Diener showed us that.
sentences.zh: 埃德·迪纳向我们展示了这一点。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: we've done some podcasts where we've talked to people about the importance of even sort of ships in the night kinds of relationships where you may just have a conversation with a stranger and how you derive benefits from that.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一些播客，讨论过即使是那种“萍水相逢”的关系的重要性，比如你可能只是和一个陌生人交谈，以及你如何从中受益。

sentences.en: So, let me ask you, then, what are the biological mechanisms that underlie the link between relationships and health?
sentences.zh: 那么，请问，人际关系与健康之间联系的生物学机制是什么？

sentences.en: You talk about relationships get under our skin.
sentences.zh: 你提到关系会“深入我们的内心”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: So, that's a tougher question to answer, in part because the science is changing so quickly on what we call biomarkers in health psychology,
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难回答的问题，部分原因是健康心理学中所谓的“生物标志物”科学发展太快了，

sentences.en: those specific physiological markers that we can assess that seem to, on the one hand, robustly predict physical health outcomes like asthma morbidity, for example,
sentences.zh: 那些我们可以评估的特定生理指标，一方面似乎能稳健地预测身体健康结果，例如哮喘发病率，

sentences.en: cardiovascular functioning, risk of heart attack.
sentences.zh: 心血管功能，心脏病发作风险。

sentences.en: And that are also associated with relationships.
sentences.zh: 而且它们也与人际关系有关。

sentences.en: And if you look at the history of health psychology, you can see if you take a snapshot of, say, 40 years ago, the hot thing was like heart rate and blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看健康心理学的历史，如果你看40年前的快照，当时的热门话题是心率和血压。

sentences.en: And then it starts moving toward different markers of the immune system 20 or 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然后20或30年前，它开始转向免疫系统的不同标志物。

sentences.en: Some of Sheldon Cohen's work, the researcher who studied the links between stress and the common cold, where he starts looking at what we call pro-inflammatory cytokines,
sentences.zh: 谢尔顿·科恩的一些工作，这位研究压力与普通感冒之间联系的研究员，他开始研究我们所谓的“促炎细胞因子”，

sentences.en: which are markers of inflammation in the immune system.
sentences.zh: 这是免疫系统中炎症的标志物。

sentences.en: We start seeing studies of cortisol.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到关于皮质醇的研究。

sentences.en: So, we've looked at all of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们已经研究了所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And I would say the most compelling evidence for relationships linking health are mortality findings.
sentences.zh: 我想说，人际关系影响健康最令人信服的证据是死亡率的发现。

sentences.en: And you see that time and time again.
sentences.zh: 你一次又一次地看到这一点。

sentences.en: Mortality is pretty easy to measure.
sentences.zh: 死亡率很容易测量。

sentences.en: Whereas when you're measuring something like pro-inflammatory cytokines from a one-shot blood draw, our cytokine levels fluctuate greatly across the day.
sentences.zh: 而当你从一次性抽血中测量促炎细胞因子之类的东西时，我们的细胞因子水平在一天中波动很大。

sentences.en: And so, it's a much less precise measure.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个精确度低得多的测量方法。

sentences.en: Having said that, we have found more positive social relationships in kids.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们在儿童身上发现了更积极的社会关系。

sentences.en: We've looked at, we have a big study that's been going on for about 10 years in Detroit, Michigan, of youth with asthma.
sentences.zh: 我们观察过，我们在底特律有一个进行了大约10年的大型研究，对象是患有哮喘的青少年。

sentences.en: And we've shown that positive parent-child relationships are associated with lower levels of inflammation in these youth.
sentences.zh: 我们已经证明，积极的亲子关系与这些青少年较低的炎症水平有关。

sentences.en: And that those levels of inflammation aren't in turn associated with better asthma symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 而这些炎症水平反过来又与更好的哮喘症状相关。

sentences.en: We've looked a lot at the stress hormone cortisol, which is naturally secreted throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 我们对压力荷尔蒙皮质醇进行了大量研究，它在一天中自然分泌。

sentences.en: It does a lot of things, primarily metabolic function, but is a good measure of stress.
sentences.zh: 它有很多功能，主要是代谢功能，但也是衡量压力的好指标。

sentences.en: We have some pretty consistent evidence that positive social relationships are associated with a steeper decline in cortisol across the day.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些相当一致的证据表明，积极的社会关系与一天中皮质醇水平更急剧的下降有关。

sentences.en: We'll have people, we've done a few studies like this, where you give people little cotton swabs to take home with them.
sentences.zh: 我们会让人，我们做过一些这样的研究，给人们小棉签带回家。

sentences.en: And over a long weekend, from say a Friday through a Monday, six times a day,
sentences.zh: 在一个长周末，比如从周五到周一，每天六次，

sentences.en: they'll chew on a little cotton swab at predetermined times to capture the circadian rhythm of cortisol.
sentences.zh: 他们在预定的时间咀嚼小棉签，以捕捉皮质醇的昼夜节律。

sentences.en: And then on those individual days, we'll either ask them about what their relationships are like,
sentences.zh: 然后在那些日子里，我们要么问他们人际关系如何，

sentences.en: or we also use this device that's an app on Android and iPhone called the electronically activated recorder or the ear to sort of take a fly on the wall perspective of people's social interactions,
sentences.zh: 或者我们也使用一种安卓和iPhone上的应用程序，叫做“电子激活记录仪”或EAR，来以一种“墙上苍蝇”的视角观察人们的社交互动，

sentences.en: which is a great objective way of tapping into relationships.
sentences.zh: 这是一种了解人际关系的极好的客观方式。

sentences.en: And either way you look at it, if it's self-reports, daily reports, or through the ear, through sound files that are coded by our research assistants,
sentences.zh: 无论你从哪个角度看，无论是自我报告、日常报告，还是通过我们的研究助理编码的声音文件（EAR），

sentences.en: you find these same kinds of effects with sort of, quote, healthier cortisol patterns being associated with healthier relationship functioning.
sentences.zh: 你都会发现同样的效应，即所谓的“更健康的皮质醇模式”与更健康的关系功能相关。

sentences.en: But are those things going to be the holy grail of our understanding of why relationships are associated with health?
sentences.zh: 但这些东西会成为我们理解为什么人际关系与健康相关的“圣杯”吗？

sentences.en: I doubt it.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示怀疑。

sentences.en: But they point, they all point in the same direction, showing that relationships are associated with health-related physiology.
sentences.zh: 但它们都指向同一个方向，表明人际关系与健康相关的生理机能有关。

sentences.en: And I think one of the most exciting things about this line of research that keeps me interested is that we're learning more and more every year about how this works from a biological standpoint.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一研究方向最令人兴奋的事情之一，也是让我保持兴趣的原因，是我们每年都在从生物学角度学到更多关于它是如何运作的知识。

sentences.en: So not all marriages are good ones, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有的婚姻都是美满的。

sentences.en: And bad marriages can also have an effect on our health.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的婚姻也会对我们的健康产生影响。

sentences.en: What are the differences between those kinds of relationships that lead to better health and well-being and those that don't?
sentences.zh: 那些导致更好健康和幸福的关系与那些不导致健康的关系之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: So that's a good question because, you know, there's this general finding that being married is good for your health.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题，因为你知道，有一个普遍的发现是“结婚对你的健康有好处”。

sentences.en: And that is, on the whole, true.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这是事实。

sentences.en: But if you dig deeper, it's much better to not be married for your health and well-being than it is to be in a bad marriage.
sentences.zh: 但如果你深入挖掘，为了你的健康和幸福，不结婚比处于一段糟糕的婚姻中要好得多。

sentences.en: And so you're asking what constitutes sort of, you know, the negative sorts of aspects of marriage that we're looking at that are associated with poor health.
sentences.zh: 所以你问的是，我们所观察到的与健康状况不佳相关的婚姻中消极方面是什么。

sentences.en: The biggest thing is conflict and how people have conflict.
sentences.zh: 最大的因素是冲突以及人们如何处理冲突。

sentences.en: Much of our work is in line with some of the classic studies in clinical and social psychology that John Gottman and others did in the lab where they found that levels of hostility in conflict discussions and low levels of positive emotions in trying to resolve conflict are associated with poor health.
sentences.zh: 我们的大部分工作与约翰·戈特曼等人在实验室中所做的临床和社会心理学经典研究一致，他们发现冲突讨论中的敌意水平和试图解决冲突时积极情绪的缺乏与健康状况不佳有关。

sentences.en: A former graduate student of mine, who's now a professor, Sabrina Byerstedl,
sentences.zh: 我的一位前研究生，现在是一位教授，萨布丽娜·拜尔斯特德尔，
zh_words: 萨布丽娜·拜尔斯特德尔

sentences.en: just published a paper last year looking at this where we had couples interacting in the lab trying to resolve a longstanding disagreement.
sentences.zh: 去年刚发表了一篇论文，我们让夫妻在实验室里互动，试图解决一个长期的分歧。

sentences.en: And, of course, they never resolve it.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们永远无法解决它。

sentences.en: But the point is to try to see how they try to resolve it.
sentences.zh: 但重点是观察他们如何尝试解决它。

sentences.en: And so we found exactly what she had predicted,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现了她所预测的完全一致的结果，

sentences.en: which was that these hostile behaviors that come out in these interactions among some couples were associated after they left the lab with dysregulated cortisol patterns in daily life with a less steep decline in cortisol throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 即在某些夫妻的互动中表现出的这些敌对行为，在他们离开实验室后，与日常生活中失调的皮质醇模式有关，即全天皮质醇下降幅度较小。

sentences.en: In other words, the cortisol stayed high for those couples.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些夫妻的皮质醇水平一直很高。

sentences.en: So I would say conflict is the big one, but also a lack of positive emotions to, you know, those intimate relationships that are lacking humor, that are lacking caring,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为冲突是最大的因素，但缺乏积极情绪也是，你知道，那些缺乏幽默感、缺乏关怀的亲密关系，

sentences.en: and that are lacking one big thing that I've looked at throughout my almost 20 years doing this research and relationships.
sentences.zh: 以及缺乏我在近20年的研究中观察到的一个重要因素。

sentences.en: And that is what we call perceived partner responsiveness.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们所说的“感知到的伴侣响应性”。

sentences.en: This is a really, really important thing for relationships, not just for your own physical health and well-being, but especially for the health of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这对人际关系来说非常非常重要，不仅是为了你自己的身体健康和幸福，尤其是为了关系的健康。

sentences.en: And so the idea here is that partners vary in the extent to which they make each other feel understood, really listened to, cared for, validated.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的想法是，伴侣在使对方感到被理解、被倾听、被关怀、被认可的程度上存在差异。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just being a good listener, but that's a big part of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不仅仅是做一个好的倾听者，但这占了很大一部分。

sentences.en: It's also being responsive to your partner's needs, being sensitive, you know, noting, knowing when they might need what we call instrumental support or, you know,
sentences.zh: 它还包括对伴侣的需求做出响应，保持敏感，你知道，注意到、知道他们何时可能需要我们所说的“工具性支持”，或者，你知道，

sentences.en: taking out the garbage, helping clean the kitchen, help take the kids somewhere, being sensitive to those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 倒垃圾、帮忙打扫厨房、帮忙带孩子去某个地方，对这些事情保持敏感。

sentences.en: Those positive aspects of responsiveness we found are really important in terms of predicting health.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这些积极的响应性方面在预测健康方面非常重要。

sentences.en: A former postdoc of mine, Sarah Stanton, had a really nice paper published a couple of years ago in the journal Psychosomatic Medicine,
sentences.zh: 我的一位前博士后，莎拉·斯坦顿，几年前在《心身医学》杂志上发表了一篇非常好的论文，

sentences.en: where she showed over a 20-year period from a large data set called Midlife in the United States,
sentences.zh: 她在其中展示了在20年期间，来自一个名为“美国中年人”的大型数据集，

sentences.en: that's at the University of Wisconsin, publicly available data of a few thousand people that perceived partner responsiveness at the very beginning of the study,
sentences.zh: 那是威斯康星大学的数据，公开了数千人的数据，研究发现研究初期感知到的伴侣响应性，

sentences.en: predicted 10 years later how people were responding to daily stressors.
sentences.zh: 预测了10年后人们如何应对日常压力源。

sentences.en: And those people who earlier, 10 years earlier, said that they had partners who are really responsive to them.
sentences.zh: 那些在10年前说他们有非常响应他们的伴侣的人，

sentences.en: Well, they were less emotionally reactive to stressors 10 years later.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在10年后对压力源的情绪反应较小。

sentences.en: So, they would have the same stressors, but they were reacting less to them.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会遇到同样的压力源，但他们的反应较小。

sentences.en: And that, in turn, 10 years after that, or 20 years from the beginning of the study, predicted lower levels of mortality.
sentences.zh: 而这反过来，在研究开始20年后，预测了更低的死亡率。

sentences.en: So, this is, you know, one of the things that I'm really interested in is not just understanding from a biological standpoint how relationships get under the skin,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我真正感兴趣的事情之一不仅是从生物学角度理解人际关系如何深入内心，

sentences.en: but from a psychological one.
sentences.zh: 而且是从心理学角度理解。

sentences.en: So, what are the, what we call mechanisms here?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们这里所说的“机制”是什么？

sentences.en: And so, emotionality seems to be a key part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，情绪性似乎是其中的关键部分。

sentences.en: We've seen that in a few different studies of ours.
sentences.zh: 我们在我们的几项不同研究中都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: But I think this is, what's so nice about this is that you have multiple time points and you can really help to better ascertain the causal direction of these things.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这非常好的一点是，你有多个时间点，你可以真正更好地确定这些事情的因果方向。

sentences.en: So, it's interesting to me that so far, sex hasn't come up.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我感兴趣的是，到目前为止，还没有提到性。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering the importance of that in relationships as well.
sentences.zh: 我想知道它在人际关系中的重要性。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't matter whether it's there, how good it is, or whether it's just about communications generally and the ability to resolve conflict.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是否存在、质量如何，或者它是否仅仅关乎一般的沟通和解决冲突的能力，这重要吗？

sentences.en: That's a really important question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的问题，金。

sentences.en: What I can tell you is that over the last 10 years, sex research, at least within social psychology and the study of relationships, has been at the vanguard.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你的是，在过去的10年里，性研究，至少在社会心理学和关系研究领域，一直处于前沿。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the most exciting research has been in the areas of sexual satisfaction and what leads to a sexually healthy relationship.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多最令人兴奋的研究都集中在性满意度和什么导致了性健康的关系这些领域。

sentences.en: And we've seen an explosion in this kind of research that when I, when the big annual meeting of social psychologists,
sentences.zh: 我们见证了这类研究的爆炸式增长，每当社会心理学家举行大型年会时，

sentences.en: we have a separate sub-meeting at the beginning of the conference for those people that study close relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们都会在会议开始时为研究亲密关系的人专门举办一场分会。

sentences.en: And there are now so many people that study sex and relationships that they have their own pre-conference.
sentences.zh: 现在研究性和关系的人太多了，他们都有了自己的会前研讨会。

sentences.en: Having said that, there's been not that much work that I'm aware of.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，据我所知，这方面的研究还不是很多。

sentences.en: And some of my colleagues who are more expert in that area of research might correct me about this.
sentences.zh: 我的一些在该研究领域更专业的同事可能会纠正我的说法。

sentences.en: But I don't know of much research that has looked at sexual satisfaction and, say, predicting mortality, for example, or some sorts of biomarkers of health.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道有多少研究探讨过性满足感与预测死亡率，或者某些健康生物标志物之间的关系。

sentences.en: But I think it's really important that we start looking at it because just so many studies have shown that sexual satisfaction is really important to relationships.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们开始关注这一点非常重要，因为已有大量研究表明，性满足感对人际关系至关重要。

sentences.en: You can be happy in a relationship where you're not terribly satisfied with your sex life.
sentences.zh: 即使你对性生活不是特别满意，你依然可以在一段关系中感到幸福。

sentences.en: But if you are really satisfied with your sex life, you're much more likely to be happy in that relationship.
sentences.zh: 但如果你对性生活非常满意，那么你在那段关系中感到幸福的可能性就会大得多。

sentences.en: That makes sense on its face.
sentences.zh: 这从表面上看是有道理的。

sentences.en: Well, let's switch for a minute and talk about technology.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们换个话题，聊聊科技。

sentences.en: You published a study a couple of years ago called Smartphones and Close Relationships, The Case for an Evolutionary Mismatch.
sentences.zh: 几年前你发表了一项研究，题为《智能手机与亲密关系：进化错配的案例》。

sentences.en: How are smartphones interfering with people's relationships these days?
sentences.zh: 如今智能手机是如何干扰人们的人际关系的？

sentences.en: Are we spending more time on our phones now than we are talking to our spouses?
sentences.zh: 我们现在花在手机上的时间比和配偶交谈的时间还多吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just a New Yorker cartoon?
sentences.zh: 还是说那只是《纽约客》漫画里的情节？

sentences.en: This has been one of the lines of research that I've been most interested in the last couple of years is how all of this new technology,
sentences.zh: 这是我过去几年最感兴趣的研究方向之一，即所有这些新技术是如何——

sentences.en: and it's still very new from an evolutionary standpoint, of course, but even in recent memory, it's still all pretty new.
sentences.zh: 当然，从进化的角度来看，它仍然非常新，即使在最近的记忆中，它也相当新。

sentences.en: How all of that impacts our relationships.
sentences.zh: 所有这些是如何影响我们的人际关系的。

sentences.en: And so from a theoretical standpoint, social media shouldn't be all that great for helping us to build close relationships.
sentences.zh: 从理论角度来看，社交媒体在帮助我们建立亲密关系方面其实并不那么出色。

sentences.en: We can build somewhat superficial relationships online, and they can become deeper if they become offline relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在网上建立某种肤浅的关系，如果它们能转化为线下关系，可能会变得更深厚。

sentences.en: But the idea that online interactions on social media are going to really foster a deep sense of connection is very much at odds with evolutionary history and why we developed to be very social creatures.
sentences.zh: 但认为社交媒体上的在线互动能真正培养出深厚的联系感，这与进化史以及我们为何进化成高度社会化生物的初衷大相径庭。

sentences.en: We developed to be social creatures in small groups, primarily dyads or groups of two or three or four people.
sentences.zh: 我们进化成社会化生物是在小群体中，主要是两人、三人或四人的群体。

sentences.en: And it's in those groups kind of only that you can really feel a sense of intimacy.
sentences.zh: 只有在这些群体中，你才能真正感受到亲密感。

sentences.en: It's hard if I'm sending out a tweet to hundreds, thousands or even millions of people.
sentences.zh: 如果我向成百上千甚至数百万人发送推文，这很难做到。

sentences.en: I'm not going to necessarily feel close to those people who are reacting to my tweet, even if it's overwhelmingly positive.
sentences.zh: 我未必会觉得与那些回应我推文的人亲近，即使回应绝大多数都是正面的。

sentences.en: It might make me feel good, but I'm not going to feel deeply connected.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让我感觉良好，但我不会感到深度连接。

sentences.en: And so that's really the evolutionary mismatch there that we have these tools that are supposed to make us feel connected.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是所谓的进化错配，我们拥有这些本应让我们感到连接的工具。

sentences.en: But at least from what we know about how relationships work, they shouldn't necessarily.
sentences.zh: 但至少根据我们对人际关系运作方式的了解，它们未必能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Now, are they bad for us?
sentences.zh: 那么，它们对我们有害吗？

sentences.en: Most of the good research out there suggests that social media use has very little impact on our well-being in terms of good or bad.
sentences.zh: 目前大多数好的研究表明，社交媒体的使用对我们的幸福感影响甚微，无论是好是坏。

sentences.en: It's sort of a net neutral.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种净中性影响。

sentences.en: There have been some really good, rigorous meta-analyses done the last couple of years where people are using better measures,
sentences.zh: 过去几年进行了一些非常出色、严谨的元分析，人们使用了更好的衡量标准，

sentences.en: more objective measures of screen time use and time spent on social media.
sentences.zh: 对屏幕使用时间和社交媒体使用时间进行了更客观的测量。

sentences.en: And when you take a step back away from self-reports, I should say self-reports, you know, if I ask you how much do you use social media and how happy you are,
sentences.zh: 当你不再依赖自我报告——我应该说自我报告，你知道，如果我问你使用多少社交媒体以及你有多快乐，

sentences.en: there's generally a small correlation between self-reported, how much I say I'm using social media, and lower well-being.
sentences.zh: 通常自我报告的社交媒体使用量与较低的幸福感之间存在微弱的相关性。

sentences.en: But when you take a step away from self-reported, people are so – they have no clue how much time they actually spend on social media.
sentences.zh: 但当你不再依赖自我报告时，人们根本不知道他们实际上在社交媒体上花了多少时间。

sentences.en: So when you actually look objectively, what we found is there's very little, if any, association, which surprised me, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以当你客观地观察时，我们发现关联性很小，甚至几乎没有，这让我感到惊讶，例如，

sentences.en: between how much couples are using their smartphones and how satisfied they are in their relationships.
sentences.zh: 在伴侣使用智能手机的频率与他们对关系的满意度之间。

sentences.en: It really seems to be when it comes to the effect of our phones on our intimate relationships, at least, it seems that the perceptions are what probably matter the moSt.
sentences.zh: 当谈到手机对我们亲密关系的影响时，至少看起来，感知才是最重要的。

sentences.en: So if you perceive that your partner is not being very responsive to you because they're on their phone all the time,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你觉得伴侣因为一直玩手机而对你不够积极回应，

sentences.en: you're probably not going to be that happy in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 你可能就不会对这段关系感到满意。

sentences.en: To what extent is that grounded in reality?
sentences.zh: 这种感觉在多大程度上是有现实依据的？

sentences.en: Small part of it is certainly grounded in reality, but a big part of it is grounded in how we see ourselves, in our personalities, how we kind of globally assess our relationship.
sentences.zh: 其中一小部分确实有现实依据，但很大一部分取决于我们如何看待自己、我们的个性，以及我们如何全面评估我们的关系。

sentences.en: You know, if I'm in a relationship that I think is really good, I'm more likely to give my partner the benefit of the doubt when asked about,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我处于一段我认为非常好的关系中，当被问及以下问题时，我更有可能给伴侣留有余地：

sentences.en: does your partner listen to you when they're on their phone?
sentences.zh: 你的伴侣在玩手机时会听你说话吗？

sentences.en: Whereas if I'm really not in a great relationship, or maybe even if I'm really annoyed at my partner that day, and you ask me that same question, I'll be like, yeah,
sentences.zh: 而如果我所处的关系并不好，或者即使那天我真的对伴侣很恼火，你问我同样的问题，我会说，是的，

sentences.en: she does seem to use her phone a lot and ignore me.
sentences.zh: 她确实好像经常玩手机而忽略我。

sentences.en: So this is one where I think we really need greater clarity on the links between online, say, social media and technologies in general and how it impacts our relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要更清楚地了解在线社交媒体、一般技术与它们如何影响我们关系之间的联系。

sentences.en: I would surmise that if there's a negative, it's mainly through taking people away from in-person social interactions.
sentences.zh: 我会推测，如果有什么负面影响，主要是因为它让人减少了面对面的社交互动。

sentences.en: So if people are spending so much time online that they're neglecting in-person social interactions, and it's positive, it can be positive in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们花太多时间在线，以至于忽视了面对面的社交互动，而它本身是积极的，那么它在很多方面都可以是积极的。

sentences.en: I mean, in finding social support, in forming connections with people that then become stronger connections offline, in forming new friendships with people generally.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在寻找社会支持、与人建立联系并转化为更强的线下关系、以及结交新朋友方面。

sentences.en: It can be, you know, there are a lot of benefits, but the negatives, I think, are less clear, and I'm becoming more murky than I am clearer about my thoughts on this.
sentences.zh: 它可以是，你知道，有很多好处，但我认为负面影响不太明确，而且我对这个问题的看法变得越来越模糊，而不是越来越清晰。

sentences.en: But again, that's kind of what makes it exciting, too.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，这也是它令人兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: You know, initially we thought social media was so bad, and now we think, ah, maybe it's not so bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最初我们认为社交媒体很糟糕，现在我们觉得，啊，也许没那么糟。

sentences.en: You know, and I tell parents this when I give talks sometimes at schools, you know, don't worry so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有时在学校演讲时会告诉家长，别太担心。

sentences.en: So if we see a couple in a restaurant, say, where they're both on their phones, it doesn't necessarily mean that they have a crummy relationship, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们看到餐厅里的一对情侣都在玩手机，这并不一定意味着他们的关系很糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不知道。

sentences.en: No, not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 不，不一定。

sentences.en: Yeah, they may be both introverts.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们可能都是内向的人。

sentences.en: They might be both trying to figure out what they're going to be ordering at the restaurant, right?
sentences.zh: 他们可能都在想在餐厅点什么菜，对吧？

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你知道。

sentences.en: Now, if you see a couple that's spending most of the meal doing that, they probably don't have a great relationship, but it's not necessarily just because of that phone use.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你看到一对情侣大部分时间都在做那个，他们的关系可能确实不太好，但这不一定仅仅是因为使用手机。

sentences.en: That phone use is probably more of a symptom than it is actually driving relationship dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 手机使用可能更多是一种症状，而不是导致关系不满的直接原因。

sentences.en: So you did another interesting study a few years ago that we might call the double date study,
sentences.zh: 几年前你做了另一项有趣的研究，我们可以称之为“双重约会研究”，

sentences.en: where you looked at how interacting with another couple affected couples' feelings for each other.
sentences.zh: 你研究了与其他情侣互动如何影响情侣之间对彼此的感情。

sentences.en: What was the impetus for that study, and what did you find?
sentences.zh: 那项研究的动力是什么？你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was one of my favorites of our studies.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是我最喜欢的我们的研究之一。

sentences.en: I did that as part of my dissertation when I was at the University of Texas,
sentences.zh: 我在德克萨斯大学攻读博士学位时做了这项研究，

sentences.en: and something that had always intrigued me that was really understudied was the effect of social networks on people's intimate relationships.
sentences.zh: 一直让我着迷且被严重低估的一个课题是社交网络对人们亲密关系的影响。

sentences.en: My wife and I have been very fortunate to have great friends that we have as a couple, and both individuals and couple friends.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子很幸运，作为一对情侣，我们拥有很棒的朋友，既有个人朋友，也有情侣朋友。

sentences.en: And, you know, this was a case maybe a little bit of what we call me-search, you know, where I wanted to figure out, you know, what is it about it?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这可能有点像我们所说的“自我研究”，我想弄清楚，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Is it that my wife and I are just happy in our relationship, and therefore we are forming more friendships together?
sentences.zh: 是因为我和我妻子在关系中很幸福，所以我们一起结交了更多的朋友吗？

sentences.en: Or is there something inherently beneficial about sharing friends with your spouse?
sentences.zh: 还是说与配偶分享朋友本身就有什么内在的好处？

sentences.en: And so the way that we did this was we brought couples, pairs of couples into the lab, and we basically provided them the context to have a really good first date.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做的方法是把几对情侣带到实验室，基本上为他们提供了一个进行非常好的第一次约会的环境。

sentences.en: We did this through a pretty neat technique that was developed by the psychologist Art Aaron called the Fast Friends,
sentences.zh: 我们通过心理学家阿特·亚伦开发的一种非常巧妙的技术来做到这一点，叫做“快速朋友”，

sentences.en: which is 45 minutes of questions that you take turns asking one another
sentences.zh: 即45分钟的问题，你们轮流问对方，

sentences.en: that increase in amount of self-disclosure.
sentences.zh: 这些问题的自我披露程度会逐渐增加。

sentences.en: So, like, the first couple of questions are just fun ones, like, if there was anybody that you could have as a dinner guest, living or dead, who would that be?
sentences.zh: 所以，前几个问题只是有趣的问题，比如，如果可以邀请任何人共进晚餐，无论在世还是已故，你会邀请谁？

sentences.en: What would constitute a perfect day for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，完美的一天是什么样的？

sentences.en: You kind of go around, and these are sort of icebreakers, but then you get into some pretty deep stuff, like, what's your relationship with your parents like?
sentences.zh: 你们会轮流回答，这些算是破冰话题，但随后会进入一些相当深刻的内容，比如，你和父母的关系如何？

sentences.en: And at the end of that, what we found was, compared to those in a small talk condition, which was pretty boring, the couples in the Fast Friends condition,
sentences.zh: 在最后，我们发现，与处于闲聊状态（相当无聊）的人相比，处于“快速朋友”状态的情侣，

sentences.en: they really felt close to the other couples.
sentences.zh: 他们确实对其他情侣感到亲近。

sentences.en: Fully a third of them, when we followed up with them a month later, became friends in real life, which I think is pretty remarkable, given, you know,
sentences.zh: 一个月后我们进行回访时，整整三分之一的人在现实生活中成为了朋友，我认为这非常了不起，考虑到，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm not sure a third of the couples I meet I want to become friends with.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我遇到的情侣中有三分之一是我愿意成为朋友的。

sentences.en: But I think what was most interesting was after this double date, people felt better about their own relationships.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最有趣的是，在这次双重约会之后，人们对自己的关系感觉更好了。

sentences.en: So, they felt closer to their romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们觉得与自己的浪漫伴侣更亲近了。

sentences.en: And in a follow-up study that was done by my former grad student, Keith Welker, we found that couples who went through the Fast Friends with other couples,
sentences.zh: 在我以前的研究生基思·威尔克所做的后续研究中，我们发现，与其他情侣一起进行“快速朋友”活动的情侣，

sentences.en: they also felt more passionately in love with their partner.
sentences.zh: 他们对伴侣的爱也更加热烈。

sentences.en: So, this kind of gets to the sexual satisfaction, you know, passion is very much tied in with that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这触及了性满足感，你知道，激情与此紧密相连。

sentences.en: And it's hard to maintain passion for your partner over time, and this seemed like it at least gave people a short-term booSt.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，很难保持对伴侣的激情，这似乎至少给了人们一个短期的提升。

sentences.en: So, the take-home for this is that double dates can be really great for your relationship, and I think that's one of those things that we really missed during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以，结论是双重约会真的对你们的关系很有好处，我认为这是我们在疫情期间真正错过的事情之一。

sentences.en: Speaking of the pandemic, let's talk for a minute about your Love in the Time of COVID project, because it's gotten a lot of media attention.
sentences.zh: 说到疫情，让我们谈谈你的“疫情时期的爱”项目，因为它受到了很多媒体的关注。

sentences.en: People are really interested in how relationships are faring through the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 人们非常关心人际关系在疫情期间的发展状况。

sentences.en: So, what have you found so far?
sentences.zh: 那么，到目前为止你发现了什么？

sentences.en: It's still ongoing, right?
sentences.zh: 它还在进行中，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you haven't…
sentences.zh: 我是说，你还没有……

sentences.en: It is still ongoing.
sentences.zh: 它确实还在进行中。

sentences.en: In fact, we're having our biweekly meeting tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们明天还要开双周会议。

sentences.en: It's given me a great source of meaning during the pandemic, and it's been really fun and interesting to be a part of this project.
sentences.zh: 它在疫情期间给了我很大的意义感，参与这个项目真的很有趣。

sentences.en: We started it at the end of March 2020, just like a week after everything shut down.
sentences.zh: 我们在2020年3月底开始了这个项目，就在一切封锁后的一周左右。

sentences.en: And it's been going since then, and we're now, I think, at our 13th wave of data collection.
sentences.zh: 从那时起它就一直在进行，我想我们现在已经到了第13波数据收集了。

sentences.en: And we have a core…
sentences.zh: 我们有一个核心……

sentences.en: We started with a ton of people.
sentences.zh: 我们开始时有很多人。

sentences.en: So, the first few waves, we have a few thousand people.
sentences.zh: 所以，前几波我们有几千人。

sentences.en: We're now down to a core group of about 500 or 600 people that have stuck with us the whole time, for which I am extremely grateful,
sentences.zh: 现在我们剩下了一个约500到600人的核心群体，他们一直坚持参与，对此我非常感激，

sentences.en: because we've learned so much about just generally what people are doing to cope better during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因为我们学到了很多关于人们在疫情期间如何更好地应对的知识。

sentences.en: And it's shown us a lot of interesting things.
sentences.zh: 它向我们展示了很多有趣的事情。

sentences.en: People who have been getting outside more during the pandemic are a lot happier.
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间更多外出的人要快乐得多。

sentences.en: People who are exercising more are happier.
sentences.zh: 锻炼更多的人更快乐。

sentences.en: And not surprisingly, relationships play a key role, especially face-to-face ones.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，人际关系起着关键作用，尤其是面对面的关系。

sentences.en: So, for those people that were able to have pods or, you know, small groups of people that they were comfortable seeing during the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些能够在疫情期间建立“泡泡”或小群体并乐于见面的人来说，

sentences.en: those in-person interactions were associated with boosts and happiness and lower levels of depression during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 那些面对面的互动与疫情期间幸福感的提升和抑郁水平的降低有关。

sentences.en: Spending time with your kids can be both a stressor during the pandemic, but also can give people a great sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 花时间陪伴孩子在疫情期间既可能是一种压力源，也能给人带来巨大的意义感。

sentences.en: Zoom was an interesting thing that we've been looking at.
sentences.zh: Zoom是我们一直在研究的一个有趣的东西。

sentences.en: That was one of those things I would never have predicted at the very beginning of the pandemic would end up being one of these things that we studied.
sentences.zh: 在疫情刚开始时，我绝不会预测到它最终会成为我们研究的对象之一。

sentences.en: But we found the smaller Zoom calls, the smaller video chats seem to be the most gratifying to people, that they feel more connected after a one-on-one,
sentences.zh: 但我们发现较小的Zoom通话、较小的视频聊天似乎最让人满足，人们在进行一对一聊天后会感到更亲近，

sentences.en: because it much more approximates an in-person social interaction than does a large Zoom call.
sentences.zh: 因为它比大型Zoom通话更接近面对面的社交互动。

sentences.en: The problem with a large video chat, even though, you know, they can have their merits, certainly, and people have had these Zoom happy hours and things like that.
sentences.zh: 大型视频聊天的问题在于，尽管它们当然有其优点，人们也举办过Zoom欢乐时光之类的活动。

sentences.en: But it's not a natural happy hour, right?
sentences.zh: 但那不是自然的欢乐时光，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, at a happy hour, you're not going to be sitting around in the circle of people going, okay, you talk next, you go next, you go next, right?
sentences.zh: 就像在欢乐时光里，你不会坐在人群中说，好吧，下一个你讲，再下一个你讲，对吧？

sentences.en: You're going to be pairing off maybe with one or two people over here.
sentences.zh: 你可能会和这里的一两个人配对聊天。

sentences.en: You know, maybe you say, okay, I'm going to go get another drink because the conversation was boring.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许你会说，好吧，我要去再喝一杯，因为谈话很无聊。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you have – it's much more organic, right?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你有——它更自然，对吧？

sentences.en: And it allows much more of a give and take.
sentences.zh: 它允许更多的互动交流。

sentences.en: Whereas online, it's really – you know, there's a lot of listening, hopefully, and just a little bit of talking.
sentences.zh: 而在网上，它确实——你知道，有很多倾听，希望如此，只有一点点谈话。

sentences.en: And so, that's why we think that the small ones are much more like the conversation you and I are having.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么我们认为小型的互动更像你我现在的谈话。

sentences.en: That's much more akin to a real-world conversation.
sentences.zh: 那更接近现实世界的对话。

sentences.en: And one of the more interesting things from our Zoom findings was that extroverts, in particular, loathe large Zoom calls because they can't talk.
sentences.zh: 我们Zoom研究中更有趣的发现之一是，外向者尤其讨厌大型Zoom通话，因为他们无法说话。

sentences.en: So, they don't have the opportunity like they would at a party to really – to have that social need met.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们没有像在聚会上那样满足社交需求的机会。

sentences.en: And also, they can't be responded to, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，他们无法得到回应，对吧？

sentences.en: I said before the importance of responsiveness.
sentences.zh: 我之前说过回应的重要性。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to feel responded to in a large Zoom call because people are distracted.
sentences.zh: 在大型Zoom通话中很难感到被回应，因为人们分心了。

sentences.en: You don't know if they're really paying attention to you.
sentences.zh: 你不知道他们是否真的在关注你。

sentences.en: The cues are not there like they would be in real life.
sentences.zh: 没有现实生活中那样的线索。

sentences.en: So, that's kind of interesting too.
sentences.zh: 所以，这也很有趣。

sentences.en: Another finding that we had was about extroversion.
sentences.zh: 我们还有另一个关于外向性的发现。

sentences.en: This reminds me, if you spend any time on Twitter, which I have from time to time, there were a lot of memes early last year about, look out for your extroverted friends.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起，如果你在Twitter上花过时间，我偶尔会去，去年年初有很多关于“照顾好你的外向朋友”的梗，

sentences.en: They're really suffering right now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在真的很痛苦。

sentences.en: And from everything that I know as a psychologist about extroversion, I thought, I don't think that's right.
sentences.zh: 根据我作为心理学家对外向性的了解，我想，我不认为那是对的。

sentences.en: I think extroverts are generally probably doing better right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为外向者目前通常可能做得更好。

sentences.en: Extroverts tend to have more energy.
sentences.zh: 外向者往往有更多的能量。

sentences.en: They tend to find creative solutions to social problems in terms of like making sure those social needs get met.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于为社交问题找到创造性的解决方案，比如确保这些社交需求得到满足。

sentences.en: Whereas introverts will often, in a situation like the pandemic, not have the inclination to sort of make the effort to stay socially connected.
sentences.zh: 而内向者在疫情这样的情况下，往往没有动力去努力保持社交联系。

sentences.en: And they tend to be a little bit lower in energy too.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的能量也往往稍微低一些。

sentences.en: So, you're not going to see people going outside as much.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不会看到他们像其他人那样经常外出。

sentences.en: And that's actually exactly what we found was that over the first three months of the pandemic, the most extroverted people showed the fewest depressive symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们发现的，在疫情的前三个月，最外向的人表现出的抑郁症状最少。

sentences.en: They showed the highest levels of happiness and meaning in life.
sentences.zh: 他们表现出最高水平的幸福感和生活意义。

sentences.en: And we found that that was at least partially explained by feeling more socially connected with other people compared to their more introverted counterparts.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，与内向的同龄人相比，这至少部分归因于感到与其他人的社交联系更紧密。

sentences.en: And also doing things like exercising more, getting outside more, all those things that we already know during the pandemic were good for people's well-being.
sentences.zh: 还有做一些事情，比如多锻炼、多外出，所有那些我们已经知道在疫情期间对人们幸福有益的事情。

sentences.en: So, yeah, lots of interesting findings.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有很多有趣的发现。

sentences.en: We have a big, it's a big international consortium at this point of a bunch of researchers working on this project.
sentences.zh: 目前我们有一个庞大的国际研究联盟，由一群研究人员共同致力于这个项目。

sentences.en: And so, we seem to have new findings every week.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们似乎每周都有新的发现。

sentences.en: One of the things we're about to look at is long-distance relationships during the pandemic, which we know very little about how distance may have impacted people.
sentences.zh: 我们即将研究的课题之一是疫情期间的异地恋，目前我们对距离如何影响人们知之甚少。

sentences.en: Well, another area where you've done some research is looking at cross-cultural relationships.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你做过研究的另一个领域是跨文化关系。

sentences.en: I know you've worked with couples in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我知道你曾与日本的伴侣们合作过。

sentences.en: What similarities or differences did you find in terms of how close relationships affect health and well-being in different cultures?
sentences.zh: 在不同文化中，亲密关系如何影响健康和幸福感，你发现了哪些相似或不同之处？

sentences.en: So, the project that I told you about where we followed, where we had data for couples over 20 years, this Midlife in the United States study in Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 关于我之前提到的那个项目，我们追踪并获取了美国威斯康星州一项名为“美国中年研究”的伴侣数据，时间跨度超过20年。

sentences.en: it turns out that there is a corollary study to it in Japan that has all of the exact same measures, age-matched with the Wisconsin sample.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，日本有一项与之对应的研究，采用了完全相同的衡量标准，且年龄段与威斯康星州的样本相匹配。

sentences.en: So, it offers a really nice opportunity for researchers to look at differences between two pretty different cultures.
sentences.zh: 因此，这为研究人员提供了一个绝佳的机会，去观察两种截然不同的文化之间的差异。

sentences.en: On the one hand, the United States, which is what we would call a more independent culture, a more individualistic culture.
sentences.zh: 一方面是美国，我们称之为更独立、更个人主义的文化。

sentences.en: And then Japan on the other, which is a more collectivistic or interdependent culture.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面是日本，这是一种更具集体主义或相互依赖的文化。

sentences.en: And so, this emerged out of a graduate course on social relationships that I teach where we were talking about responsiveness.
sentences.zh: 这源于我教授的一门关于社会关系的硕士课程，当时我们正在讨论“响应性”。

sentences.en: And one of the PhD students in the class said, you know, Rich, you keep talking about how important responsiveness is in people's intimate relationships.
sentences.zh: 班上一位博士生说：“Rich，你一直在谈论响应性在人们亲密关系中的重要性。”

sentences.en: But I lived in Japan for a few years.
sentences.zh: “但我曾在那边生活过几年。”

sentences.en: And the outside relationships, outside the intimate relationships, so relationships with family members especially, seem to be a lot more important.
sentences.zh: “而亲密关系之外的社交关系，尤其是与家庭成员的关系，似乎要重要得多。”

sentences.en: And she said, I just think that responsiveness is going to matter less for people's happiness there than it would here.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我觉得在那里，响应性对人们幸福感的影响不如在这里那么大。”

sentences.en: And so, she did some preliminary analyses and I bumped into a very close colleague at a meeting who I've published a few papers on responsiveness with.
sentences.zh: 于是她做了一些初步分析，后来我在一次会议上偶遇了一位亲密的同事，我们曾就响应性共同发表过几篇论文。

sentences.en: And I told him about this idea and he said, you're not going to believe it.
sentences.zh: 我告诉了他这个想法，他说：“你绝对想不到。”

sentences.en: We're looking at that exact same question.
sentences.zh: “我们正在研究同一个问题。”

sentences.en: And so, we joined forces to look at this.
sentences.zh: 于是我们联手对此进行了研究。

sentences.en: And what we found was, as my student initially had thought, there were differences.
sentences.zh: 正如我学生最初所想的那样，我们发现确实存在差异。

sentences.en: Now, responsiveness in your relationship still was associated with greater well-being in Japan.
sentences.zh: 在日本，伴侣间的响应性仍然与更高的幸福感相关。

sentences.en: But not to the same extent as it is here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但程度不如在美国这里这么高。

sentences.en: How responsive your intimate partner is seems to matter a lot more because we put so much weight on our intimate relationships.
sentences.zh: 你的亲密伴侣有多大的响应性似乎非常重要，因为我们把太多的重心放在了亲密关系上。

sentences.en: Eli Finkel has done some really nice work in this area, the social psychologist at Northwestern University, who's written a book called The All or Nothing Marriage.
sentences.zh: 西北大学的社会心理学家Eli Finkel在这个领域做了非常出色的工作，他写了一本书叫《全或无的婚姻》（The All or Nothing Marriage）。

sentences.en: And he has hypothesized that in Western society over the last 100 years or so,
sentences.zh: 他假设在过去100年左右的西方社会中，

sentences.en: the intimate relationship has been almost an exclusive focus for us in terms of for those that are in intimate relationships for pathways to happiness and meaning in life.
sentences.zh: 对于那些处于亲密关系中的人来说，亲密关系几乎成了我们寻求幸福和人生意义的唯一焦点。

sentences.en: In other words, we are expecting more and more from our intimate partners in terms of helping us to be happy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们对亲密伴侣的期望越来越高，希望他们能帮助我们获得幸福。

sentences.en: And for those marriages that are incredibly happy and bring us meaning, people seem to be highly self-actualized, and to use terms of Abraham Maslow.
sentences.zh: 对于那些极其幸福并能带来意义的婚姻，人们似乎达到了亚伯拉罕·马斯洛所说的“高度自我实现”。

sentences.en: Whereas those couples where they're not getting those needs, self-esteem needs and those kinds of needs that deal with the core self, those kinds of needs met,
sentences.zh: 而对于那些无法满足这些需求——即自尊需求以及涉及核心自我的需求——的伴侣来说，

sentences.en: that they're miserable at the extremes.
sentences.zh: 极端情况下，他们会感到非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And our data seem to suggest that, yes, that is more true here than in countries like Japan, where there's not as much pressure on intimate partners to satisfy all of your needs.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据似乎表明，是的，这种情况在这里比在日本等国家更真实，因为在日本，伴侣满足你所有需求的压力并没有那么大。

sentences.en: You know, the family, the extended social network is more important there than it is here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在那里，家庭和更广泛的社交网络比在这里更重要。

sentences.en: And I think there's a lesson to be learned there, you know, that maybe we're putting too much pressure on our relationships to make us happy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中有一个教训，也许我们给亲密关系施加了太大的压力，要求它们让我们幸福。

sentences.en: So, keying off of that, we've been talking a lot about research and theory.
sentences.zh: 那么，以此为切入点，我们已经谈了很多关于研究和理论的内容。

sentences.en: So, let me ask a question for our listeners who might be interested in more practical advice and wisdom that they can draw from your research.
sentences.zh: 我想为那些可能对从你的研究中汲取更多实用建议和智慧感兴趣的听众问一个问题。

sentences.en: Last question, what are the most important things people can do to improve their relationships and become better partners?
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，人们为了改善关系、成为更好的伴侣，最重要的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Excellent question to end on that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的结束问题。

sentences.en: So, try to be as responsive a partner as you can.
sentences.zh: 首先，尽量做一个有响应性的伴侣。

sentences.en: And that starts with being a good listener to your partner.
sentences.zh: 这始于做一个好的倾听者。

sentences.en: You know, when you come home from work, put the phone down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，下班回家后，把手机放下。

sentences.en: When your partner makes a bid for your attention, really try to pay attention to them.
sentences.zh: 当你的伴侣试图引起你的注意时，一定要试着去关注他们。

sentences.en: And then more broadly, to try to be sensitive to their needs.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，要试着对他们的需求保持敏感。

sentences.en: But I think being a really good listener is a key part of that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为做一个好的倾听者是其中的关键。

sentences.en: One of the things that we know is a good booster for relationships is what we call novel and exciting activities.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，促进关系的一个好方法是进行所谓的“新奇且令人兴奋的活动”。

sentences.en: Try something new together.
sentences.zh: 一起尝试一些新事物。

sentences.en: You know, and there's lots of things that will seem new now that we're coming out of the pandemic that we haven't done for a long time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，随着疫情结束，有很多我们很久没做过的事情现在看起来都很新鲜。

sentences.en: But, you know, go on a hike together.
sentences.zh: 比如，一起去徒步旅行。

sentences.en: Go on a double date together.
sentences.zh: 一起进行双人约会。

sentences.en: Or just go on a date to a restaurant you haven't tried.
sentences.zh: 或者只是去一家你们没去过的餐厅约会。

sentences.en: Trying new things that are fun can be a boost to people's relationships.
sentences.zh: 尝试有趣的新事物可以促进人们的关系。

sentences.en: For parents out there, and I have some friends that are new parents,
sentences.zh: 对于那些为人父母的朋友，我有一些刚当父母的朋友，

sentences.en: it's really important to maintain that connection and to try to do things with your spouse to try to keep that connection going.
sentences.zh: 保持那种联系，并尝试与配偶一起做些事情来维持这种连接是非常重要的。

sentences.en: Because the strength of those two parent families comes from the strength of their relationship.
sentences.zh: 因为双亲家庭的力量源于他们关系的稳固。

sentences.en: And the importance of social networks.
sentences.zh: 还有社交网络的重要性。

sentences.en: You know, if you're finding that you and your partner don't do a lot with friends together,
sentences.zh: 如果你发现你和伴侣很少一起和朋友互动，

sentences.en: I would suggest that they look at that and see if there are ways that they can branch out a bit.
sentences.zh: 我建议你们审视一下，看看是否有办法稍微拓展一下社交圈。

sentences.en: Maybe have some, you know, some work colleagues and their spouses over to your place or neighbors.
sentences.zh: 也许可以邀请一些同事和他们的配偶，或者邻居到家里来。

sentences.en: Because they can be so enriching for our relationships.
sentences.zh: 因为这能极大地丰富我们的关系。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Dr. Slotcher.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，Slotcher博士。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有趣。

sentences.en: I appreciate all of your insights and hearing about your research, which is just fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我很感谢你的见解，也听到了你的研究，这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Well, it's been fun for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说也很愉快。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或 Apple、Stitcher 以及任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢我们，请留下评论。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。
